title: Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 1,344 - The Hindu
description: Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 1,344  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
The death toll due to the devastating flash floods in Nepal rose to 1,344 on Saturday (September 5, 2026) as more bodies were recovered from the affected areas while thousands remain missing, police said.

According to the data released by the Nepal Police, a total of 843 bodies have been successfully recovered, consisting of 758 adults and 85 children.

Also read | Nepal’s agony, the Himalayan warning to India

Additionally, authorities also reported having retrieved 501 amputated bodies from the flood-hit areas.

The death toll in the flash floods on Saturday (September 5, 2026) rose to 1,344 with the recovery of more bodies, Nepal Police said in a statement.

Nepal floods: 5-year-old among three Indians rescued from Trishuli Bazaar area

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal, leaving a trail of destruction.

So far, 1,030 bodies have been managed by temporarily burying them underground as per specified regulations such as DNA collection.

The joint rescue teams led by the Nepal Army have continued their search and rescue efforts on the eleventh day on Saturday, with the number of missing people estimated at 4,898.

full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of people still missing.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued on Friday.

Nepal's army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-meter (about 740-foot) tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel.

Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing and roughly 500 are believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said. Specialized rescue ​teams from India, China, South Korea and the United States have been searching through debris, damaged structures and tunnels at the projects, hoping to find survivors.

In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was being airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.

Images released by Nepal’s army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket.

At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

___

Saaliq reported from New Delhi. Associated Press journalist Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.

title: Two survivors pulled from Nepal tunnel - The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
description: Two survivors pulled from Nepal tunnel  The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
publisher.title: The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette
full_article:
Let us read it for you. Listen now. Your browser does not support the audio element.

KATHMANDU, Nepal -- Rescuers pulled two survivors from a tunnel linked to a hydropower station on Nepal's Trishuli River on Friday, nine days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through its valley, killing more than 1,300 people and leaving over 5,600 missing.

Officials and rescue workers said they believe the August 26 collapse of a glacier on the upper reaches of the river trapped at least 900 people in tunnels related to six hydropower projects.

The two workers pulled from the tunnel at the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station are the first to be rescued from the hydropower projects and have been taken to an army hospital in the capital Kathmandu, giving search teams a flicker of hope as the possibility of finding other survivors fades. The army said they had also recovered a body from the site.

Videos released by Nepali authorities showed Kabir Maharjan being hoisted from a hole in the ground as bystanders cheered, then lowered onto a stretcher. His colleague Sanjay Sah was brought out on a worker's back, his face still caked in mud, before army doctors fitted an oxygen mask and checked his vitals inside a rescue tent.

Sah, a mechanical foreman, later described staying behind in a control room in a tunnel to help others escape after he urged colleagues to flee upon hearing news of the disaster.

"I was in the control room, so my responsibility was to save everyone's lives. When there was such a big accident, it was not right for me to run away," he said in a video recording shared by Nepali authorities.

Sah told rescuers he spent time reciting mantras while he was trapped. He said he had been in contact with three or four more people in the tunnel, while others could still be alive deeper in its reaches.

Nepal's army said it had recovered two bodies from a tunnel at Langtang Hydropower Station.

At least 1,294 people have been killed in Nepal in the floods that swept away houses, streets and schools in towns and villages near the border with Tibet, the disaster management authority said on Friday. More than 5,053 are still missing, including 583 foreign nationals, many of them pilgrims and trekkers.

China on Friday raised the death toll in Tibet to 31, with 531 others listed as missing, according to state media Xinhua.

The two rescued men are now in intensive care at an army hospital and their vital signs are stable, a source from the facility told Reuters. Mechanical supervisor Maharjan cannot move his hands or legs, but Sah's injuries are not considered critical, according to an aide to the energy minister.

A team of experts in a WhatsApp group was guiding rescue workers in the search at the hydropower projects in what has become a valuable tool alongside helicopters and heavy machinery in the race to find survivors.

More search and rescue operations were underway around the Upper Trishuli 3A project, the Nepali army said. Rescue efforts were being led by the army and police, with assistance from experts from India, South Korea and China.

Property, housing and infrastructure worth at least $2.56 billion were lost in last week's catastrophe, Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, said on Friday.

Nepal will need to rebuild around 20,000 houses in flood-ravaged areas, Upreti has said, with at least 7,500 of those homes destroyed.

Information for this article was contributed by Yukun Zhang.

नेपाली अधिकारी द्वारा जारी वीडियो मे कबीर महर्जन के जमीन के छेद स लहराबैत देखल गेल अछि, जखन कि दर्शक जयकार करैत छल, फेर स्ट्रेचर पर उतारल गेल छल। हुनकऽ सहयोगी संजय साह क॑ एगो मजदूर के पीठ प॑ बाहर लानलऽ गेलै, जेकरऽ चेहरा अखनी भी थाल-कादो स॑ केक होय गेलऽ छेलै, ओकरा स॑ पहल॑ सेना केरऽ डॉक्टर न॑ ऑक्सीजन मास्क लगाय क॑ रेस्क्यू टेंट के भीतर ओकरऽ वाइटल के जांच करलकै ।

full_article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of people still missing.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued on Friday.

Nepal's army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-meter (about 740-foot) tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel.

Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing and roughly 500 are believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said. Specialized rescue ​teams from India, China, South Korea and the United States have been searching through debris, damaged structures and tunnels at the projects, hoping to find survivors.

In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was being airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment.

Images released by Nepal’s army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket.

At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

Saaliq reported from New Delhi. Associated Press journalist Kanis Leung in Hong Kong contributed to this report.

देश केरऽ प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय केरऽ सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट के अनुसार ई आदमी क॑ जलविद्युत सुरंग स॑ बचालऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ कुल तीन मजदूर त्रिशुली जलविद्युत परियोजना स॑ जिंदा खींचलऽ गेलऽ छै । शुक्रदिन २ नेपाली मजदूरके उद्धार भेल अछि ।

नेपालके सेना नेपाली सेनाकर्मी आ दक्षिण कोरियाके आपदा विशेषज्ञके संयुक्त बचाव दल २२५ मिटर (करीब ७४० फीट) के सुरंगसँ ओ आदमीके उद्धार केने अछि आ ओकर स्वास्थ्य आकलन चलि रहल अछि । छवि में देखलऽ गेलऽ छै कि हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ हुनका बाहर निकाललऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ सेना केरऽ मेडिकल उड़ान के दौरान हुनकऽ हालत के जांच करी रहलऽ छेलै ।

चीनी सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी द्वारा जारी फोटो मे देखल गेल अछि जे दू टा बचावकर्मी ओहि आदमी के सुरंग सं बाहर ल जा रहल छल.

अधिकारि सब कहलनि जे, बचाव कार्य पूरा नेपाल मे 12 टा जलविद्युत परियोजना पर बेसी ध्यान देल गेल अछि, जतय करीब 900 मजदूर लापता अछि आ मोटा-मोटी 500 मजदूर विभिन्न सुरंग मे फंसल हेबाक आशंका अछि। भारत, चीन, दक्षिण कोरिया आरू अमेरिका केरऽ विशेष बचाव टीम परियोजना सब प॑ मलबा, क्षतिग्रस्त संरचना आरू सुरंगऽ के माध्यम स॑ खोज करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ ई उम्मीद छै कि बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ मिलतै ।

बाढ़ि प्रभावित नुवाकोट शहर मे एकटा महिला के एकटा घर स जीवित बचाओल गेल, नेपाल के सेना के प्रवक्ता शनिदिन कहलनि। अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, हुनका इलाज के लेल हवाई जहाज सं काठमांडू पहुंचाओल जा रहल अछि।

नेपाल के सेना द्वारा जारी तस्वीर मे बचावकर्मी के क्षतिग्रस्त घर के भीतर महिला के थाल मे ढंकल भेटल अछि. धूसर रंगक कम्बल मे लपेटल सुरक्षित स्थान पर खींचबा सँ पहिने ओकरा बोतलबंद पानि देलक।

नेपाल के आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार 26 अगस्त के बाढ़ि मे कम सं कम 1300 लोक के मौत भ गेल छल, जे संभवतः ग्लेशियर के गिरला सं भेल छल आओर 5000 सं बेसि लोक लापता अछि.

सालिक नई दिल्ली स रिपोर्ट केलनि। हांगकांग केरऽ एसोसिएटेड प्रेस केरऽ पत्रकार कनिस लेउंग न॑ ई रिपोर्ट म॑ योगदान देल॑ छै ।

title: Nepal tunnel rescue revives hopes 10 days after flood - France 24
description: Nepal tunnel rescue revives hopes 10 days after flood  France 24
publisher.title: France 24
full_article:
A joint rescue team comprising personnel from the Nepal Army and foreign experts rescued the man from 225 metres (738 feet) inside the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district, a military statement said.

A picture of the rescue published on the army's Facebook page shows the man, identified only as Luhaitao, with his arms around the shoulders of two camouflage-clad rescuers.

He looked alert but his hands were covered in thick, slimy mud.

"His health is currently being assessed and further search and rescue operations are continuing," the army said.

The survivor was among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on August 26.

Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors © Prakash MATHEMA / AFP

Two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued on Friday at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continued alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods.

So far, 1,344 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the national disaster agency, with around 5,000 people missing.

In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing. That takes the overall death toll to 1,375 people, and more than 5,500 missing.

Thousands in relief camps

Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP that "work is underway at the tunnels" to locate any survivors.

The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.

Rescuers called it a "miracle" after the two Nepali men, caked in mud, were pulled out alive on Friday, nine days after being trapped by the flood.

A rescue helicopter flies as Army personnel and members of Nepal Scouts install a zip-line across the Trishuli River in the aftermath of flash floods © Arun SANKAR / AFP

They were taken to hospital and are said to be in a stable condition.

Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside blocked tunnels.

With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies hade been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, Nepal Police said Saturday.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah promised to provide "safe and comfortable accommodation" for thousands of people displaced by the diaster and currently living in temporary relief camps.

"We know that staying there (in camps) is not easy for you," he said in a Friday post on social media.

But he promised to "once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future".

In Nepal, rescuers pulled out alive a Chinese citizen who had been in a tunnel connected to a hydropower project on the Trishuli. This was the third successful rescue from tunnels at Trishuli hydropower facilities after the floods.

Joint rescue operation

As NDTV World reports, the operation was carried out by Nepalese military personnel together with South Korean emergency response specialists. The man was extracted from a 225-meter-long tunnel. He was flown by helicopter for a medical examination.

Two Nepalese workers were rescued the previous day from the tunnel of the Trishuli-3A hydropower plant. Overall, rescuers have found four people alive in flood-affected areas in recent days.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

Consequences of the floods

In the city of Nuwakot, rescuers also saved 64-year-old Chandika Shrestha, who was found in a damaged house. According to officials, she was flown to Kathmandu by helicopter for treatment.

According to the authorities, nearly 900 workers remain missing at 12 hydropower projects in Nepal. About 500 of them may be in various tunnels, officials estimate. The floods of August 26, likely caused by a glacier collapse, claimed at least 1,300 lives. According to Nepal's emergency management agency, more than 5,000 people are still considered missing.

KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of people still missing.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued on Friday.

Nepal’s army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-meter (about 740-foot) tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel.

A man and a woman have been found alive 10 days after the devastating floods near the Nepal-Tibet border, officials said.

Images of the man and woman being rescued were posted by Nepal's Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers on Saturday, confirming the rescues.

The man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country's prime minister's office. Three workers in total have now been pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project, the Associated Press said.

Two other Nepali workers were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday, according to AP..

At least 557 workers are missing from the Trishuli 3A hydropower project along the Trishuli River, with about 115 believed to be trapped in the tunnel, according to the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

Nepal's Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina said officials remain hopeful that more workers will be rescued. "We are waiting for the rescue of more and more people," Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page.

Meanwhile, in flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday.

The death toll following last week's unprecedented flash flood at the Nepal-Tibet border has climbed to 1,344, with an additional 4,996 people believed to still be missing as of Saturday, officials said.

Chinese state media have reported an additional 16 deaths and 546 missing people in Tibet.

Two people were rescued in separate operations in Nepal, 10 days after the devastating floods hit the country, officials said Saturday.

A man was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post by the country's prime minister's office, bringing the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday.

Nepal's army said a joint rescue team of Nepalese military personnel and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from 738-foot tunnel and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.

Chinese national seen after being rescued by soldiers during an ongoing operation at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project in Nepal's Rasuwa district, Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026. / Credit: Nepal Army/AP

A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel.

Rescue efforts have increasingly focused on 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, where about 900 workers are missing and roughly 500 are believed to be trapped in various tunnels, authorities said. Specialized rescue teams from India, China, South Korea and the United States have been searching through debris, damaged structures and tunnels at the projects, hoping to find survivors.

In flood-hit Nuwakot town, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal's army spokesperson said Saturday. Officials said she was being airlifted to Kathmandu.

Images released by Nepal's army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud. They gave her bottled water before pulling her to safety, wrapped in a gray blanket.

At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal's disaster management agency.

बाढ़ि प्रभावित नुवाकोट शहर मे एकटा महिला के एकटा घर स जीवित बचाओल गेल, नेपाल के सेना के प्रवक्ता शनिदिन कहलनि। अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, हुनका हवाई जहाज सं काठमांडू पहुंचाओल जा रहल अछि।

नेपालक सेना द्वारा जारी कएल गेल तस्वीर मे बचावकर्मी के महिला के थाल मे आच्छादित भेटल अछि। धूसर रंगक कम्बल मे लपेटल सुरक्षित स्थान पर खींचबा सँ पहिने ओकरा बोतलबंद पानि देलक।

नेपाल के आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के अनुसार 26 अगस्त के बाढ़ि में कम सं कम 1300 लोक के मौत भ गेल छल, जे ग्लेशियर के गिरला सं भेल छल आ 5000 सं बेसी लोक लापता अछि.

full_article:
Members of the Nepal Army search and rescue team carry a Chinese national after he was rescued alive from a tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project following devastating floods and mudslides, in Rasuwa, Nepal, Sept 5, 2026. (NEPAL ARMY/HANDOUT VIA REUTERS)

KATHMANDU – Nepali rescuers on Saturday rescued a Chinese national from a hydropower plant hit by the deadly mudslide in Nepal, according to the Chinese Embassy in Nepal.

The Chinese national was rescued by the Nepali Army in coordination with a disaster expert team from South Korea, 10 days after a devastating mudslide struck the area.

The survivor was taken for further medical assessment and care.

The rescue is part of an intensified effort to locate and evacuate people believed to be trapped inside hydropower project tunnels following a mudslide that swept through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems.

The disaster caused extensive damage to several hydropower projects and other infrastructure in the affected areas. Some workers and other people are believed to have been trapped inside hydropower tunnels and have remained out of contact.

According to the latest details released by the Nepal police, as many as 1,344 bodies had been recovered by 5 am local time on Saturday. Police said 4,898 people remained out of contact as of Saturday morning, and 8,631 people have been rescued.

Before the rescue of the Chinese national, the Nepali Army said in a social media post that a joint rescue team comprising 20 Nepali Army personnel and project representatives had been conducting search operations.

The Nepali Army has been conducting search and rescue operations in coordination with foreign technical teams, including experts from China, India and South Korea, to reach people stranded inside structures at several hydropower projects.

64-year-old Nepali woman rescued

A 64-year-old Nepali woman was also rescued alive on Saturday in Nuwako district.

After initial treatment, the woman will be transferred to the capital, Kathmandu, for further treatment, according to the media.

काठमाण्डु – नेपालमे भेल घातक कीचड़सँ प्रभावित जलविद्युत संयंत्रसँ नेपाली उद्धारक नेपाली उद्धारकर्ता शनिदिन एकटा चीनी नागरिकके उद्धार केने अछि ।

चीन के नागरिक के दक्षिण कोरिया के आपदा विशेषज्ञ टीम के समन्वय में नेपाली सेना के तरफ सं बचाओल गेल छल, जखन कि इलाका में भयावह कीचड़ के झटका लागल छल.

बचि गेल व्यक्ति के आगू के मेडिकल आकलन आ देखभाल के लेल ल गेल गेल।

ई बचाव भोटेकोशी आरू त्रिशुली नदी प्रणाली म॑ बहलऽ कीचड़ के बाद जलविद्युत परियोजना के सुरंगऽ के भीतर फंसलऽ मानलऽ जाय वाला लोगऽ के पता लगाबै आरू ओकरा खाली करै के तेज प्रयास के हिस्सा छेकै ।

एहि आपदा स प्रभावित इलाका मे कईटा जलविद्युत परियोजना आ अन्य बुनियादी ढांचा कए काफी नुकसान पहुंचेलक। मानल जा रहल अछि जे किछ मजदूर आओर दोसर लोक जलविद्युत सुरंग के अंदर फंसल छथिन्ह आओर संपर्क सं बाहर रहय छथिन्ह.

नेपाल प्रहरी द्वारा जारी ताजा विवरण के अनुसार शनिदिन स्थानीय समय के अनुसार भोर ५ बजे तक १,३४४ शव बरामद भेल अछि । पुलिस के कहनाय अछि जे शनिदिन भोर धरि 4898 लोक संपर्क सं बाहर अछि, आओर 8631 लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि.

ग्योरोंग बंदरगाह के पास खोज आब गहींर, बेसी लक्षित

चीनी नागरिकके उद्धारसँ पहिने नेपाली सेना सोशल मिडिया पोस्टमे नेपाली सेनाके २० जवान आ परियोजना प्रतिनिधिसभक संयुक्त बचाव दल खोजबीन कार्यरत रहल बतौलक अछि ।

नेपाली सेना चीन, भारत आ दक्षिण कोरिया के विशेषज्ञ सहित विदेशी तकनीकी टीम के समन्वय स खोज आ बचाव अभियान क कईटा जलविद्युत परियोजना मे संरचना के भीतर फंसल लोक तक पहुंचैत आबि रहल अछि।

६४ वर्षीय नेपाली महिलाके उद्धार

नुवाको जिल्लामे शनिदिन ६४ वर्षीय नेपाली महिलाके सेहो जिन्दा उद्धार कएल गेल अछि ।

प्रारंभिक उपचार के बाद महिला के आगू के इलाज के लेल राजधानी काठमांडू में स्थानांतरित कयल जायत, मीडिया के अनुसार।
